facts.statement: The genus Vallibonavenatrix is a spinosaurid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous found in the Arcillas de Morella Formation of Castellón, Spain.
facts.quote: Vallibonavenatrix (meaning "Vallibona huntress" after the town near where its remains were found) is a genus of spinosaurid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) Arcillas de Morella Formation of Castellón, Spain.

facts.statement: Elisabete Malafaia and colleagues formally described the species Vallibonavenatrix cani in 2019 based on a partial skeleton.
facts.quote: In 2019, Elisabete Malafaia and colleagues published their description of a new genus and species of spinosaurid dinosaur, Vallibonavenatrix cani, with the partial skeleton as the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: The generic name Vallibonavenatrix combines the town of Vallibona with the Latin word for huntress.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the town of Vallibona, with the Latin suffix "-venatrix", meaning "huntress".

facts.statement: The specific name 'cani' honors Juan Cano Forner, the amateur fossil collector who discovered the remains.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Cano Forner, the fossil's discoverer.

facts.statement: Vallibonavenatrix is the most complete spinosaurid fossil found on the Iberian Peninsula.
facts.quote: Vallibonavenatrix represents the most complete spinosaurid specimen recovered from the Iberian Peninsula.

facts.statement: Vallibonavenatrix was a moderately sized bipedal predator.
facts.quote: Vallibonavenatrix was a moderately-sized bipedal predator.

facts.statement: Vallibonavenatrix had moderately tall dorsal neural spines, one of which was expanded into a trapezoidal, fan-like shape similar to Ichthyovenator.
facts.quote: The upwards-projecting neural spines of its dorsal vertebrae were moderately tall, and one known spine is expanded from bottom to top in a trapezoidal, fan-like shape, similar to those of the spinosaurid Ichthyovenator.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the morphology of Vallibonavenatrix's neural spines may have formed a sail on its back.
facts.quote: Similarities between the morphology of the neural spines of these two taxa may indicate the presence of elongated spines forming a sail on Vallibonavenatrix's back, as is seen in some other spinosaurids.

facts.statement: The sacrum of Vallibonavenatrix featured deep depressions and air-filled pneumatic openings.
facts.quote: The sacrum of Vallibonavenatrix had deep pleurocoelous fossae (depressions) and pneumatic (air-filled) openings.

facts.statement: The ilium of Vallibonavenatrix was highly pneumatic with large internal chambers.
facts.quote: The ilium of the pelvis was also highly pneumatic, and had large internal chambers.

facts.statement: Vallibonavenatrix lived during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous, between 129.4 and 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: Vallibonavenatrix hails from the Arcillas de Morella Formation, which has been dated to the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous period, between 129.4 and 125 million years ago.

facts.statement: Vallibonavenatrix shared its environment with Iguanodon bernissartensis, Morelladon beltrani, an indeterminate sauropod, and the spinosaurid Protathlitis.
facts.quote: It coexisted in this environment with other dinosaurs including the ornithischians Iguanodon bernissartensis and Morelladon beltrani, an indeterminate sauropod, and fellow spinosaurid Protathlitis.

facts.statement: In 2019, Malafaia and colleagues classified Vallibonavenatrix within the family Spinosauridae.
facts.quote: In 2019, Malafaia and her team classified Vallibonavenatrix within the Spinosauridae, a family of large-bodied tetanuran dinosaurs traditionally separated into two subfamilies: Spinosaurinae and Baryonychinae.

facts.statement: Malafaia and colleagues found Vallibonavenatrix more closely related to spinosaurines like Spinosaurus and Irritator than to baryonychines like Baryonyx.
facts.quote: Though closer in proximity to European baryonychines such as Baryonyx from the Barremian of Spain and England, Vallibonavenatrix was found to be more closely related to spinosaurines such as Spinosaurus and Irritator from the southern supercontinent Gondwana, and the Asian genus Ichthyovenator.

facts.statement: Based on their analysis, Malafaia and colleagues placed Vallibonavenatrix within the subfamily Spinosaurinae.
facts.quote: Thus, Malafaia and colleagues placed it within Spinosaurinae.

facts.statement: A 2021 study by Chris Barker and colleagues found Vallibonavenatrix's phylogenetic position unstable, placing it either as the most basal spinosaurid outside both subfamilies or within Baryonychinae depending on the analysis method.
facts.quote: However, in 2021, Chris Barker and colleagues instead found Vallibonavenatrix in one of two positions, depending on the type of analysis (parsimony-based or Bayesian) that they performed: outside of both Spinosaurinae and Baryonychinae as the most basal (least specialized) spinosaurid, or as a member of the Baryonychinae.

facts.statement: Certain anatomical characteristics suggest Vallibonavenatrix may have an affinity with spinosaurines rather than baryonychines.
facts.quote: However, certain anatomical characteristics may indicate an affinity with that group, rather than with the baryonychines.

facts.statement: A 2025 reassessment by Rauhut and colleagues recovered Vallibonavenatrix within Spinosaurinae, diverging after Iberospinus.
facts.quote: Spinosaurine affinities were supported in a 2025 reassessment of Camarillasaurus by Rauhut and colleagues, who recovered Vallibonavenatrix within the Spinosaurinae, diverging after Iberospinus.

facts.statement: Vallibonavenatrix was a moderate-sized bipedal predator.
facts.quote: Vallibonavenatrix era un depredador bípedo de tamaño moderado.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that similarities in neural spine morphology may indicate Vallibonavenatrix had elongated spines forming a sail on its back.
facts.quote: Las similitudes entre la morfología de las espinas neurales de estos dos taxones pueden indicar la presencia de espinas alargadas que forman una vela en la espalda de Vallibonavenatrix, como se ve en algunos otros espinosáuridos.

facts.statement: The sacrum and ilium of Vallibonavenatrix contained deep pleurocoelous fossae and pneumatic openings filled with air.
facts.quote: El sacro de Vallibonavenatrix tenía profundas fosas pleurocelosas y aberturas neumáticas, llenas de aire. El ilion de la pelvis también era muy neumático y tenía grandes cámaras internas.

facts.statement: Remains of Vallibonavenatrix were found in the Arcillas de Morella Formation in Castellón province, Spain.
facts.quote: Sus restos se hallaron en la Formación Arcillas de Morella en la provincia de Castellón en España.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is a partial skeleton consisting of a cervical vertebra, six dorsal vertebrae, an almost complete sacrum, fragments of neural spines, four caudal vertebrae, ten partial ribs and rib fragments, three incomplete chevrons, an almost complete left ilium, fragments of the ventral part of a right ilium, incomplete right and left ischia, and a fragment thought to belong to the proximal part of the pubis.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo es un esqueleto parcial consistente en una vértebra cervical, seis vértebras dorsales, un sacro casi completo, fragmentos de neuroapófisis, cuatro vértebras caudales, diez costillas parciales y fragmentos de costillas, tres cheurones incompletos, un ilion izquierdo casi completo, fragmentos de la parte ventral de un ilion derecho, isquiones derecho e izquierdo incompletos, y un fragmento que se piensa es perteneciente a la parte proximal del pubis.

facts.statement: Elisabete Malafaia and colleagues described the new genus and species Vallibonavenatrix cani in 2019.
facts.quote: En 2019, Elisabete Malafaia y sus colegas publicaron su descripción de un nuevo género y especie de dinosaurio espinosáurido, Vallibonavenatrix cani, con el esqueleto parcial como espécimen holotipo.

facts.statement: The genus name references the town of Vallibona and the Latin suffix "-venatrix", meaning "hunter".
facts.quote: El nombre del género hace referencia al pueblo de Vallibona, con el sufijo latino "-venatrix ", que significa "cazadora".

facts.statement: The specific name honors Cano Forner, the discoverer of the fossil.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honra a Cano Forner, el descubridor del fósil.

facts.statement: Vallibonavenatrix represents the most complete spinosaurid specimen recovered from the Iberian Peninsula.
facts.quote: Vallibonavenatrix representa el espécimen de espinosáurido más completo recuperado de la península ibérica.

facts.statement: Vallibonavenatrix lived at the beginning of the Cretaceous period, approximately 130 to 125 million years ago during the Barremian, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a principio del período cretácico, hace aproximadamente 130 a 125 millones de años durante el Barremiense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: The Arcillas de Morella Formation, where Vallibonavenatrix was found, is dated to the Early Cretaceous Barremian, between 129.4 and 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: Vallibonavenatrix procede de la Formación Arcillas de Morella, que se ha fechado en el Barremiense del Cretácico Inferior , hace entre 129,4 y 125 millones de años.

facts.statement: The time range for Vallibonavenatrix is recorded as the Barremian, from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 2019, Malafaia and her team classified Vallibonavenatrix within Spinosauridae, a family of large-bodied tetanuran dinosaurs traditionally divided into two subfamilies, Spinosaurinae and Baryonychinae.
facts.quote: En 2019, Malafaia y su equipo clasificaron a Vallibonavenatrix dentro de Spinosauridae, una familia de dinosaurios tetanuros de cuerpo grande tradicionalmente separados en dos subfamilias, Spinosaurinae y Baryonychinae.

facts.statement: In 2021, Chris Barker and colleagues found Vallibonavenatrix in one of two positions depending on the analysis type: outside Spinosaurinae and Baryonychinae as the most basal, less specialized spinosaurid, or as a member of Baryonychinae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 2021, Chris Barker y sus colegas encontraron a Vallibonavenatrix en una de dos posiciones, según el tipo de análisis, basado en parsimonia o bayesiano, que realizaron: fuera de Spinosaurinae y Baryonychinae como el espinosáurido más basal, menos especializado, o como miembro de Baryonychinae.

facts.statement: Barker and colleagues concluded that its phylogenetic position was unstable.
facts.quote: Llegaron a la conclusión de que su posición filogenética era inestable.

facts.statement: A study by Octávio Mateus and Darío Estraviz-López in 2022 also did not find Vallibonavenatrix to be a spinosaurid.
facts.quote: Al igual que los resultados de Barker et al., un estudio de 2022 de Octávio Mateus y Darío Estraviz-López no encontró que Vallibonavenatrix sea un espinosáurido.

facts.statement: However, certain anatomical features may indicate an affinity with spinosaurids rather than baryonychids.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, ciertas características anatómicas pueden indicar una afinidad con ese grupo, más que con los barioniquinídos.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Vallibonavenatrix as Baryonychinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Baryonychinae

facts.statement: Vallibonavenatrix coexisted with other dinosaurs including the ornithischians Iguanodon bernissartensis and Morelladon beltrani, an indeterminate sauropod, and an indeterminate baryonychid.
facts.quote: Coexistió en este entorno con otros dinosaurios, incluidos los ornitisquios Iguanodon bernissartensis y Morelladon beltrani , un saurópodo indeterminado y un barioniquinído indeterminado.

facts.statement: During the late 1980s and early 1990s, amateur fossil collector Juan Cano Forner recovered bones from various localities in the Els Ports Natural Park in Castellón province, Spain.
facts.quote: Durante finales de la década de 1980 y principios de la de 1990, el coleccionista aficionado de fósiles Juan Cano Forner estuvo recuperando huesos de varias localidades del Parque Natural de Els Ports, ubicado en la provincia de Castellón, España.
